newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Poll shows Australian govt lead narrows.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Poll shows Australian govt lead narrows.

text.p: The opinion poll lead held by Australia's Liberal-National government over the Labor opposition has narrowed slightly in an opinion poll published in Tuesday's edition of The Australian newspaper.

The government's primary support rose one percentage point from The Australian's last poll five weeks ago to 49 percent, while Labor's support increased two points to 38 percent, The Australian's Newspoll found.
As preferred prime minister, John Howard's lead over opposition leader Kim Beazley increased to 32 points from 29 points in the last poll.
Howard's rating as preferred prime minister increased one point to 54 percent, while Beazley's rating fell two points to 22 percent.
The latest result compares with the government's primary vote of 47.3 percent and Labor's 38.8 percent in the March 2 national election that ended 13 years of Labor rule.
The Newspoll surveyed 1,148 voters around the country by telephone over the last weekend.
The Sydney Morning Herald's AGB-McNair poll also found Howard had narrowed its opinion poll lead over the Labor opposition.

Primary support for the Liberal-National government fell three percentage points to 44 percent from the previous poll seven weeks ago, while Labor's support fell two points to 35 percent, the AGB-McNair poll found.
Two-party preferred support for the government fell one percentage point to 53 percent from the previous poll, while Labor's support rose one point to 47 percent, the poll found.
As preferred prime minister, Howard's lead over Beazley was unchanged at 25 points in the last poll.
Howard's rating as preferred prime minister fell one percentage point to 54 percent, while Beazley's rating fell one point to 29 percent.
The AGB-McNair poll surveyed 1,956 voters nationwide by telephone over the last weekend.
